transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

## Why it trips about 15 minutes in

On most dishwashers, about 10 to 20 minutes into a cycle is when the water heater switches on. A trip that happens at that point, but not every time, points strongly to a heating element with an earth leakage fault. When the element's internal insulation starts breaking down, it leaks a small current to earth once it's hot and wet, and the RCD trips. It's often intermittent at first and gets worse over time.

On this Zanussi/Electrolux design the heater is usually built into the circulation (wash) pump, often called a "heat pump" assembly. So the fix is normally replacing that whole unit rather than a separate element.

## First, check what's actually tripping

Look at your consumer unit:

• RCD trips (the switch with a "T" test button, often covering several circuits): this means earth leakage. It fits the heater theory and is the most likely case.
• MCB trips (the individual circuit breaker): this means overload or short circuit, which is less typical. It could point to a dead short or too much else running on the same circuit.

## Quick checks you can do yourself

1. Plug it straight into a wall socket. Don't use an extension lead or adaptor, and if you can, try a different socket or circuit.
2. Run a cycle with no heat, such as a rinse or pre-rinse, if your model offers one. If it never trips on that but trips on a hot wash, that's further evidence the heater is at fault.
3. Look for leaks. Check under and around the machine and the bottom of the door. Water dripping onto the wiring or the base, for example from a worn door seal or a leaking sump or pump seal, can cause the same symptom.
4. Check the base tray. If the machine has ever shown a flood or leak error, or the drain pump runs constantly, there may be water sitting in the base.
5. Rule out the RCD itself. If other appliances on the same RCD (kettle, washing machine, etc.) also run at the same time, the small leakages can add up. Try running the dishwasher with less else on.

## Getting a definite diagnosis

A normal multimeter often won't catch this kind of fault. The proper test is an insulation resistance test with a "megger" on the heater/pump. Any appliance engineer or electrician can do it quickly.

## Safety

• Always unplug it before looking inside or removing panels.
• Don't keep resetting it and running it. Repeated earth faults are what the RCD is protecting you from.
• If you're not comfortable with this, an appliance repair engineer can confirm the fault and fit the part.

## Is it worth repairing?

The heat pump part typically costs around £50–£100 online; search the model number plus "heat pump" or "circulation pump with heater". The repair is usually worthwhile if the machine is otherwise in good condition. If it's quite old and a professional repair would cost £150 or more all-in, it may be worth comparing that against the price of a new machine.

If you can tell me whether it's the RCD or the MCB tripping, and whether it ever trips on a short or cool cycle, I can help narrow it down further.

It's the RCD in the consumer unit that trips, a whole bank of circuits goes off including the kitchen. Never trips on a quick cold rinse, only on the hot washes like the 65C one. I'm not keen on taking any covers off though.

That pattern (RCD trips, only on hot washes, never on a cold rinse) all but confirms an earth leakage fault in the heating circuit. The most likely culprit is the heater in the wash pump assembly. Since you'd rather not take covers off, the next step is a repair engineer, and that's a sensible choice here since the fix involves mains wiring and water.

## In the meantime

• Avoid hot washes. The RCD is doing its job by cutting power when current leaks to earth, but repeatedly tripping and resetting it isn't a good idea. A faulty element can get worse.
• Cold rinses are probably fine if you need them, but ideally leave the machine off until it's looked at.
• If you notice burning smells, scorch marks, or water around the base, unplug it and don't use it at all.

## Getting it repaired

Who to call:
• Zanussi/Electrolux's own service (book via the Zanussi UK website). They use genuine parts and are useful if you have any warranty or extended cover.
• A local independent appliance engineer. They're often cheaper and quicker. Check reviews, or look for someone registered with a trade body.
• Check first whether you have appliance cover through home insurance, a retailer extended warranty, or a scheme like Domestic & General.

What to tell them: "RCD trips about 15 minutes into hot washes only, never on cold rinse. Suspect heater/heat pump earth leakage." That helps them bring the right part. A good engineer will do an insulation resistance test to confirm it before replacing anything.

Rough UK costs (these vary by area):
• Replacement heat pump part: roughly £60 to £130
• Fitted by an engineer, including call-out and labour: typically £130 to £250 total

## Repair or replace?

The ZDT21006FA is a fairly basic model and isn't new. A new comparable dishwasher costs around £250 to £350. So:
• If the machine is otherwise in good shape and the repair quote is under about £150 to £180, repairing is usually worth it.
• If it's quite old or has other issues, or the quote is near the price of a new one, replacing it may make more sense.

Ask the engineer to diagnose it and quote before doing the work, so you can decide.
